extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: Two sets of reliable labels for the tiny images dataset. The CIFAR-10 set has 6000 examples of each of 10 classes and the CIFAR-100 set has 600 examples of each of 100 non-overlapping classes.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by searching the web for images of non-abstract English nouns from WordNet using search engines like Google, Flickr, and Altavista, keeping the first 3000 results per term, and filtering out duplicates and mostly white images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 80 million color images downscaled to 32x32 pixels, distributed across 79,000 search terms.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset's original labels, which are based on search terms, are highly unreliable, making the raw dataset difficult to use for object recognition without manual labeling. Additionally, the raw data contained perfect duplicates and synthetic figures (identified by excessively white pixels) that had to be filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for unsupervised training of deep generative models and pre-training feature layers. The labeled subsets (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) are specifically used to train classifiers for object recognition experiments.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was subsetted for unsupervised learning experiments, and images were divided into patches and subsampled.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were downscaled, filtered for duplicates and excessive white pixels, whitened, and had their least significant directions of variance removed.
